**Key passages to check:**

1. Pequod description — many signature phrases
2. "A cannibal of a craft" extended passage
3. The Quaker digression leading to "all mortal greatness is but disease"
4. Peleg/Bildad dialogue — the 777th lay comedy
5. "He's a grand, ungodly, god-like man" passage
6. Ahab's wife / "Ahab has his humanities"
7. Closing Ishmael meditation
8. Yojo description and Queequeg's fasting scene

Let me go through carefully:

**Yojo passage:** Source has a notable aside about Yojo being "a rather good sort of god, who perhaps meant well enough upon the whole, but in all cases did not succeed in his benevolent designs." This ironic, voice-establishing aside is **absent** from the draft.

**Pequod name etymology:** "Pequod, you will no doubt remember, was the name of a celebrated tribe of Massachusetts Indians; now extinct as the ancient Medes." The "now extinct as the ancient Medes" phrase is dropped — the draft says only "named after the extinct tribe." This is a signature phrase with interpretive weight (ominous naming motif).

**"She was apparelled like any barbaric Ethiopian emperor"** — the draft has this in paraphrase form ("apparelled like a barbaric Ethiopian emperor, pendants of polished ivory") — partially preserved.

**"She was a thing of trophies. A cannibal of a craft, tricking herself forth in the chased bones of her enemies."** — The draft has "a cannibal of a craft, tricking herself in the chased bones of her enemies" — "forth" dropped, "She was a thing of trophies" present as fragment. Acceptable compression.

**Helmsman/Tartar tiller:** Source: "The helmsman who steered by that tiller in a tempest, felt like the Tartar, when he holds back his fiery steed by clutching its jaw." Draft: "The helmsman in a tempest felt like a Tartar clutching his steed's jaw." — flattened but present.

**"A noble craft, but somehow a most melancholy! All noble things are touched with that."** — Present verbatim. ✓

**Quaker digression / "all mortal greatness is but disease":** Source has an extended passage about Scripture-named men blending Quaker idiom with Scandinavian sea-king daring, culminating in "a mighty pageant creature, formed for noble tragedies" and "Be sure of this, O young ambition, all mortal greatness is but disease." The draft **preserves most of this** but clips "receiving all nature's sweet or savage impressions fresh from her own virgin voluntary and confiding breast" — "voluntary and confiding" dropped. Minor. The core "all mortal greatness is but disease" is present. ✓

**Bildad description:** Source has the memorable "Indolence and idleness perished before him. His own person was the exact embodiment of his utilitarian character. On his long, gaunt body, he carried no spare flesh, no superfluous beard, his chin having a soft, economical nap to it, like the worn nap of his broad-brimmed hat." Draft has only "tall, gaunt, drab to the chin" — this signature characterization of Bildad's "utilitarian" person with the "economical nap" is **absent**.

**"Lay not up for yourselves treasures" wordplay** — the extended punning meditation on "lay" is significantly compressed in the draft. The source has Ishmael's extended internal monologue: "_Lay_, indeed, thought I, and such a lay!... thou art determined that I, for one, shall not _lay_ up many _lays_ here below... the seven hundred and seventy-seventh part of a farthing is a good deal less than seven hundred and seventy-seven gold doubloons." This comic wordplay on "lay" is a signature passage — **absent** from the draft.

**"Thou Bildad!" roared Peleg** speech about conscience — "thy conscience may be drawing ten inches of water, or ten fathoms... thy conscience be but a leaky one; and will in the end sink thee foundering down to the fiery pit" — this Bildad retort is **absent** in the draft, going straight to Peleg's outrage. The nautical metaphor of conscience drawing water is a signature voice passage.

**Peleg's description of Ahab:** "He's a grand, ungodly, god-like man, Captain Ahab" — present ✓. The full speech is mostly preserved.

**"it's better to sail with a moody good captain than a laughing bad one"** — present ✓

**"Ahab has his humanities!"** — present ✓

**Closing meditation** — largely verbatim ✓

**"now extinct as the ancient Medes"** — absent, reduced to "extinct tribe"

**Yojo as "rather good sort of god who perhaps meant well enough"** — absent

**Bildad's "economical nap" / utilitarian body description** — absent

**The lay wordplay passage** — absent

**Bildad's conscience/leaky-one retort** — absent

The lay wordplay is clearly a signature passage — Ishmael's comedic voice at its most ironic, with the punning on "lay" being a set-piece. Its absence is a voice erasure.

Bildad's "leaky conscience" nautical metaphor is distinctive voice material.

"now extinct as the ancient Medes" is an interpretive/ominous naming motif.
